en: Preface to the Recorded Sayings of Master Gulin, Compiled by Feng Zizhen, Court Gentleman and Former Attendant at the Bureau of Scholarly Worthies.

Rare sounds require the valley to transmit their resonance; awakening from delusion through a fleeting shadow must rely upon a mirror for clarity. When seeking one’s own head in a mirror, [one finds...]
The valley receives the resonance. The valley has a mouth, yet the mirror has no mind. Sound cannot be pursued by footprints; a reflection cannot be stepped upon by traces.
As for grasping it with the intention, there is a distant perception of its form-like appearance;

as for responding to it through the sensory realm, there is a profound realization that there is neither coming nor staying. A sudden call is answered immediately; the West sings and the East harmonizes. Is this not so?
Is this not the transmission of the Valley? Affection does not enhance the beauty of a face, nor does hatred diminish its lack of beauty.
Is this not the clarity of the mirror?
Master Gulin of Baoning in Jinling occupied four seats of enlightenment, benefiting all beings; eminent monks from the five directions [gathered there].

With their conical hats aligned and their knees level as they moved sideways on tiptoe, they crossed their shoes and galloped in four directions. When they emerged, there was discourse; when they discoursed, there was recording.

The resonance of their voices reached out like a valley responding to a call; their clarity was like a mirror reflecting an image. As the apertures opened and the whistling flutes sounded, ten thousand ravines shook in unison.
When defilements are exhausted, luminosity returns; not even a speck of dust can settle there. It is like the medicinal tree on the Snowy Mountains:
one wishes to smell it, yet the sense of smell awakens as spring turns back. It is like the *sudha* bowl of India: one intends to hold it, yet the fragrance overflows from the crown of the head.

Swift as a flash of lightning, crashing like a thunderclap across a clear sky; a divine spade cleaving a waterfall, leveling highways and deepening abysses. When flowers bloom upon the White Rock of the North, what need is there for another peak?

In their mutual encounter, the plum fruits ripen south of Mount Dayu; all behold the vying ascent to the other shore. Sinu Gu picks up the theme once more, and the subsequent arrow suddenly startles one with its bitten barb.
Tongzong continues the lineage again; let the lead horse wait a moment while you urge the whip. The vast ocean becomes a bubble and a grain of rice within a single tide;
Mount Sumeru is but a clod of earth and a lotus fiber spanning billions of kalpas. Thus, those who wear the scholar’s cap and girdle shall transform their decayed and rotten [bodies].
Observing those who carry their staffs and robes, whose chests are purified by ritual ablutions, the pines remain green through the snow and the grasses remain verdant amidst the frost.
As for the *Essentials of Huangbo*, Pei Xiu ought to have composed a preface to reveal its innermost core. Danxia’s aspirations lie afar; in my old age, I lack the vigor to shave my beard and hair.

For now, I shall recount what is currently seen at Fengtai, while still seeking to glimpse the lingering echoes of the Deer Park. Jiang Xi-ping drank from the waters of Pang Hengyang; this did not hinder his tasting [the truth].
I, Qin Mazu, offer this stone tribute to Elder Yuan. Su Gong, with his dull faculties, was moved to laughter; I have roughly cited the beginning of his intent and performed this rite of worship.
On the day of the winter solstice, the year of Yichou, during the Taiding era.

On the third day of the second month in the second year of the Dade era, the Master [entered the hall] at the front hall of Chengtian Nengren Chan Monastery.
At the Head Seat’s Quarters, having accepted the invitation, he entered the monastery and pointed to the mountain gate, saying: "The doors and windows stand wide open; who is it facing the hall?
Red clouds pierce the azure void; the white sun encircles Mount Sumeru."

The Master said: "One blow and it is accomplished; filling the valleys and bridging the ravines, no blow is required. Supporting heaven and propping up earth—those without nostrils need not smell the fragrance;
those with throats are made to breathe out. Where Li Lou walks, the waves overflow the heavens;
at the bottom of the great ocean, there is not a drop of water. He gave a shout.
Pointing to the Dharma seat, he said: "If you say this seat is too high or too wide, it is no more than seven or eight feet.
It is simply because you all exert yourselves too much that you are unable to ascend it. What does this have to do with Mount Sumeru or King Lamp? [Having said this,] he then ascended the seat."

Holding up the incense, he said: "This single portion of incense is burned within the burner specifically to pray for the longevity of the present Emperor—ten thousand years, ten thousand years, ten thousand times ten thousand years!

May Your Majesty’s benevolence be as vast as that of Yao and your virtue ever renewed like that of Tang. May you live as long as the lifespan of a mustard seed, and establish a great legacy that endures as long as the stone is struck."

[He] prostrates. Next, he holds up the incense and says: "When the Buddhas appeared in the world, they transmitted mind-to-mind; when the Patriarch came from the West, he entrusted the Dharma-to-Dharma.

Mind and Dharma are non-dual, penetrating throughout the ten directions. Later, as the monastic groves declined and the Buddha-Dharma became diluted, the elders of various quarters who appeared in the world each used incense as a token of their credentials.
But what 'credentials' does incense possess? One should know that true credentials do not [reside in external objects]."

It resides in fragrance, yet it resides in the Dharma. On this day of the Tianping era, this incense is burned within the burner, offered in honor of the late Abbot Hyanggwon, the tenth-generation successor of Yangqi, the Great Master of Gwangri Seon Temple on Ayuwang Mountain.

"I shall merely present my offerings; what more need be said? Having said this, he took his seat. After the head monk had struck the gavel, a monk asked: "When the Buddha Mahābhijñājñānābhibhū sat at the site of enlightenment for ten kalpas, yet the Buddha-dharma did not manifest before him and he could not attain the Way of Buddhahood—what was that like? The Master said: "He would have required another ten kalpas before he could attain it. The monk pressed further: "When one has the spirit, one adds to that spirit. The Master replied: "Not so. The monk asked again: "What about when one lacks the spirit? The Master said: "It is not that there is no spirit. The monk asked: "If there is no spirit, how can there be anything to add? The Master said: "It is not that there is nothing to add. The monk asked: "How is it then? The Master said: "It is simply that there is no such thing as 'adding'. "Where there is elegance, there is elegance. The Master said, "Be careful not to seek it from others; otherwise, you will remain far removed from me.

The student asked, "Just as when the World-Honored One appeared in the world in the past, followed by Śakra and Brahmā—when the Master opens the hall today, what auspicious signs are there ultimately?
The Master said, "Mount Sumeru is beneath your feet. The student said, "If that is so," [the Master continued: "Then..."
The imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace are both repaid at once. The Master said, “May we rejoice that the world is at great peace.
A monk asked, “When Baoshou opened the hall, Sansheng pushed forward a monk, and Baoshou struck him immediately. What was the meaning of this?
The Master said, “A snake does not move without a head. The monk pressed further, “Sansheng said, ‘If you act as a teacher in such a manner, you will not only blind this monk’s eyes...’”
"You have blinded the eyes of the entire city of Zhinzhou! Baoshou threw down his staff and returned to his quarters.
"How about this? The Master said, "Seven blows for thirteen. The student asked, "Even before you left Shuang'e, I had already heard of this essential pivot.
The Master said, "Why is it that when one arrives here, there is none? The student said, "To withdraw oneself and yield to others."
"One in ten thousand. The Master said, "Come back tomorrow and I will give you a blow of my staff. The monk bowed.
The Master then said, "Stop your questioning for a moment; you must know that [this] is before you have even entered the gate."
The imperial grace and the Buddha’s grace are both repaid at once. [The Master] strikes the whisk and says:

"This Dharma cannot be understood through thought, deliberation, or discrimination. To the south of heaven and the north of earth, the sun, moon, and stars, walls, fences, tiles, and pebbles—all are free from the four propositions and transcend the hundred negations.
At this moment, people know it exists. From the Deer Park to the end at the Nairañjanā River, it is ultimately..."
What matter does this clarify? It is what is called "the Buddhas handing it down hand-to-hand" and "the patriarchs transmitting it from one to another.

A single phrase, manifest before us, cuts off the ten directions in a single stroke. At such a time, how is it? A thousand peaks bow toward Mount Hua; ten thousand streams flow solemnly into the Canglang River.
Again, he cites Master Bodhidharma, who said: "I have come to this land to transmit the Dharma and save deluded beings.

One flower opens into five petals; the fruition is naturally accomplished. He then strikes the meditation staff and says: "Clouds move and rain falls; the three types of grass and two types of trees [all flourish]."
Ascending the hall, he said: "The myriad dharmas are fundamentally at rest; it is only people who create their own clamor.

Let pass Linji and Deshan; beat to death Yunmen and Xueqiao. Setting aside for a moment the fact that the entire earth is the adamantine eye—putting away the dustpan and broom—why does Hanshan clap his hands and laugh so loudly?
A vast marsh conceals mountains; principle can subdue a leopard."
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the case of Zen Master Xuedou, who said: "The spring mountains layer upon layer of chaotic green; the spring waters ripple with empty azure.
Vast and silent between heaven and earth, standing alone, what can one gaze upon to the limit? The Master said: "Excellent, great assembly!

It is truly not in vain that Mañjuśrī and Samantabhadra were banished to the two Iron Ring Mountains for giving rise to views of Buddha and views of Dharma. Some say that Xuedou was selling husks along with the grain."
Noodles. Their value lies in a single moment. Yet, one does not realize that while the eyes look toward the southeast, the mind is set upon the northwest.
The flowing spring drips steadily; the white rocks are sharp and distinct. Clouds drift in fragments, emerging in the morning and returning at night;
the sun shines radiantly, rising in the east and setting in the west. (He strikes the whisk once.)
Ascending the hall on the Buddha’s Birthday, he suddenly took up his staff and said, "From birth until death, it is only this. As for Old Śākyamuni, what is he?
A dried piece of excrement. He then descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked: "One is not it; two is not it. When the third-tier waves rise high, the fish transforms into a dragon; yet the deluded person still scoops water from the night pond.
As a student, I have come before you; I beg the Master for instruction. The Master said: "No one knows this meaning; it makes me remember Nanquan. The monk pressed further:
"The flowers must bloom through the night; do not wait for the morning breeze to blow. The Master said: "Tighten your belt! (or: "Be more diligent!")
[The Master] holds up a straw sandal. The monk prostrates. The Master then says: "The ancients said, 'If you discuss this matter, you must brandish the sword;

if you do not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in his hut. Therefore, from the beginning, whether Buddha or Patriarch, whenever they presented a single pivot or revealed a single realm, there was nothing that did not penetrate the subtle and the profound depths.
This is what is called pulling out the nails and extracting the wedges, untying the glue and removing the bonds. Know this."
As for those who know it directly, it is simply that the kindness is so great it is difficult to repay. As for those who do not know it, how are they any different from carving ice or chiseling snow?
In this place of mine, the phrase that cannot be uttered even with one’s full strength is neither on Lion Peak nor within Lake Tai;
it is beneath the feet of you all, where it is pierced through in seven places and perforated in eight. From where have you obtained it? (He lets out a shout.)
Ascending the hall, he said: "The ox of the open ground has been cooked; the sun is at its zenith. The gate of the unconditioned true nature opens the path that reaches through the heavens.
Since the path to heaven is opened, I invite everyone to enter through this very place. Therefore it is said:

'If I head toward the mountain of blades, the mountain of blades shall crumble of itself; if I head toward the cauldron of boiling water, the cauldron of boiling water shall dry up of itself. Tsk! Tsk!"
"Alas! There is nothing with which it can be compared.
How am I to speak of it? He ascended the hall and raised an example: Yanquan asked a monk, "Where have you come from? The monk replied, "From Daochang. Yanquan said, "What place is this?
The monk said, "A thief does not strike a poor man's house. Fenyang, acting on his behalf, said, "Simply strike him as he speaks."

The Master said: "Thieves do not strike the homes of the poor. Why, then, do they strike here? Only when you possess the eye of discernment here can you understand that the ancients’ arrows never miss their mark."
Ascending the hall, he heard the sound of the bell and donned his seven-piece robe. Seeing the sun rise and shine upon the straw mats, he said:
"The affairs of daily life are ordinary; why need one seek elsewhere? The Samādhi of the World-Honored One was not known by Kāśyapa; the Samādhi of Kāśyapa was not known by Ānanda;
the Samādhi of Ānanda was not known by Śāṇakavāsin. Raising up his staff, he said: "The staff!"
Samādhi. No one knew [the meaning]. Master Zhuo held up his staff and said: "When the dragon obtains water, his spirit increases; when the tiger encounters mountain scenery, his fierce majesty grows.

He ascended the hall and cited the story of National Teacher Niu-tou, who personally prepared the meals to provide for the assembly of monks. Whenever it was time for the midday meal, he would carry [the food] out...
The Rice Bucket went before the hall; he performed a dance and said, "Sons of Bodhisattvas, come eat! Then he clapped his hands and laughed loudly.
Xuedou commented, "Even so, Niu-er was not acting with good intentions. The Master said, "Xuedou wrongly applied these words;
at that time, was it not 'Righteousness Bringing Abundant Harvests'?"
Ascending the hall, he said: "How far away is the Way? It is true in every encounter. How distant are the sages? They are divine as soon as one embodies them.
The dense yellow chrysanthemums cannot but be called Prajñā; the verdant green bamboos cannot but be called Dharmakāya."
Therefore, at the ground of the ultimate reality (*bhūtakoṭi*), not a single speck of dust is accepted; within the gateway of the myriad practices (*sāhasra-caryā*), not a single dharma is abandoned.
Whether you all believe this or do not believe it, thirty years from now, when you encounter a practitioner of true substance, do not say:
"The style of the White Cloud Gate is steep and formidable; in the end, one cannot grasp it. Descent from the seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "The ancients said: 'When lifted up, heaven revolves and earth turns; when set down, the grass bows and the wind blows.
Leaving aside these two paths, what is the Master’s way of benefiting others? The Master said, "There are no three days of hiding within the grass.
The monk stepped forward and said, "I see only the white clouds flying and scattering; I do not know upon whose house the bright moon has fallen. The Master said, "Zhu-tu! (A grunt of affirmation).
[The Master] pinned it on his nostrils. Furthermore, a monk asked: "What is 'taking away the person but not the environment'?

The Master said: "In the early morning there is congee; at the midday meal there is rice. The monk asked: "What is 'taking away the environment but not the person'? The Master said: "If you wish to eat, let him eat;
if you do not wish to eat, go wherever you please. The monk asked: "What is 'taking away both person and environment'? The Master said: [He remained silent.]
"The lantern swallows the pillar. The monk asked, "How is it when both the person and the environment are not taken away?
The Master said, "The kitchen and storehouse stand exactly opposite the monks' hall. The monk bowed. The Master then said: "The rooster crows in broad daylight;
the ocean waves surge. The dog barks at twilight; Mount Sumeru stands towering. To drag over the kingdom of Campā and join it with the forehead of Silla—this I do not ask about."
The mountain birds gather; the ox wags its tail. Among the three hundred assemblies of Śākyamuni, in which assembly did he ever preach this Dharma?
At this point, were it not for the clear penetration of the eye of wisdom, one would immediately lose sight of it by a thousand miles.
Nevertheless, when I, this mountain monk, speak thus, I am merely suppressing the truth to accommodate you.
Ascending the hall, he raised the example of Master Panshan, who said: "It is like throwing a sword into the air; one need not discuss whether it reaches its mark or not.
This is because the empty wheel leaves no trace, and the blade of the sword is not diminished. If you can be thus, then mind after mind is without knowing. The Master said:

In the east they sell at a high price; in the west they sell at a low price. The Nāga King of Lake Anavatapta invited the Buddha for a meal, and the Venerable Piṇḍola Bhāradvāja was also included among the number. He descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall: When going downhill, one does not run; such a swift opportunity is difficult to encounter. If it comes from the east, strike from the east; if it comes from the west, strike from the west;

if it comes from all four directions and the eight points, strike back with the staff. Now tell me, did the ancients have any way of benefiting others? You blind fellows, do not harbor deluded thoughts!
In the past, when I heard this Dharma, I never proclaimed it recklessly. Deshan [once] cut down his own wooden plaque.
In a bustling marketplace, whose hearth has no smoke? Drawing a winnowing fan with red earth—the matter arises from such instructions. [The Master] descends from his seat.
He ascends the hall and cites Yunmen: “The Dharma-body eats food; the illusory, empty body is itself the Dharma-body. Vast as heaven and earth!”
Where does the ground exist? Not a single thing can be apprehended; one is merely swallowing emptiness with emptiness.
If one were to examine this closely, it would seem that such talk ought to be possible. The Master said, "It may be so, but for now, there is no principle of the Buddha-dharma in it."
The illusory, empty body is itself the Dharmakāya. Are not heaven and earth and the great land the Dharmakāya?
Not a single thing can be grasped; one uses emptiness to consume emptiness. Yet even emptiness cannot be grasped. When examined from this perspective, one cannot even save oneself.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "All obstacles are ultimate awakening; whether mindfulness is attained or lost, there is nothing that is not liberation.
Raising his whisk, he said: "Every person possesses this. Why then do they fail to use it? For this reason, the Buddhas appear in the world and the Patriarchs come from the West;
it is nothing other than to cause people to recognize this very thing before the existence of either birth or Buddhahood."
"Not this. "Three pounds of flax. "A dried-up shit-stick. "Under the Zhanglei Mountain, a bamboo-rattan whip.
"The opening is not upon the tongue. He lets out a shout and says: "When I press my finger, the Sea-Seal emits light; when you briefly raise your mind, worldly toil arises first.
If you can recognize it here, the Old Śākyamuni, by the power of his original vow, manifested in Jambudvīpa."

He elevates those in the four modes of birth and serves as a bridge and a vessel for the nine realms of existence. May every person realize and witness the natural splendor of their original ground, becoming an eye and a mirror for humanity and the heavens.
After a long silence, he lets out another shout and says: "Two released, three cast aside; six seated, seven walking.
The whole family is sent off on the ferry at the riverhead. Nine times nine remains eighty-one. He then descends from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "All obstacles are ultimate awakening. He then struck the meditation staff and declared: "Without the spring breeze, the flowers would not bloom;
yet once they have bloomed, they are blown down by the wind. He then descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised the example of the Venerable Ship’s Master, who said: “A thousand-fathom silk line hangs straight down; A single ripple stirs, and ten thousand waves follow.
The night is still and the water cold, yet the fish do not bite; The boat returns empty under the bright moon. The Master said: “Excellent, great assembly!
Now, in your discussions, you all say that the ancients labored in vain and achieved nothing. Little do you realize that across those ten thousand miles of misty waves—”
The intent lies with the *kūn* and the *jīng*. A single scale or a tiny fin merely exhausts itself on the hook. Thus does the white cloud announce it: do you all know where it lands?
To cite the ancients and the present—whom would they not understand? When the strings are moved, the melody changes; those who can appreciate it are rare.
(He strikes the whisk and descends from his seat.)
Ascending the hall, the Master said: "The Patriarch said: 'The ground of the mind contains all seeds; when the universal rain falls, they all sprout.
Once the nature of the flower is suddenly realized, that which was about to be born is immediately unborn.

As for the thirty-three heavens, the twenty-eight lunar mansions, the five thousand and forty-eight fascicles [of the scriptures], and the aspects of teaching, principle, practice, and fruition—does this principle exist within them or not? The lanterns dance, the pillars raise their brows. Two...
A Vajra deity bursts into laughter: "A pair of red apricots are traded for a persimmon. Entering the hall, he said:
"Great wisdom is profoundly clear, like a pearl on a platter; it turns of its own accord without being pushed. For one who has attained thorough understanding, not even a single point is required.
Therefore it is said: sometimes there is illumination first and then function; sometimes there is function first and then illumination."
At times illumination and function are simultaneous; at other times illumination and function are not simultaneous. Linji’s little lad, however, possesses a single eye.
Although the ancients spoke thus, even if they were to reach up to the Brahma Heaven, when one examines them closely, it is much like using shrimp as eyes.
[The Master] suddenly brandishes his staff and says: "Light does not see darkness; darkness does not see light. When both light and darkness are forgotten..."
"What is this? He lets out a shout and says, "Leaping and bounding upon Mount Sumeru! Then he claps his hands and laughs heartily.

Everyone’s nostrils point toward the vast heavens, yet it is simply because they have not realized what is right before their eyes. [The Master] strikes the sounding block once and ascends the hall, saying:
"Good assembly! 'A fragrant breeze blows from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool. Old Miaoxi struck it here, bumping against it—how could this be considered anything extraordinary?

Baoyun said: 'A fragrant breeze blows from the south; the halls and pavilions grow..."* *(Note: The source text appears to be a fragment of a recorded discourse (*yulu*). The final sentence is left incomplete as it was in the original.)*
A slight coolness. The short is simply short; the long is simply long. Fundamentally, there is neither delusion nor enlightenment; how could it involve discursive thought?
Where does the boundless small boat go? At nightfall, it was never in the Xiang or Xiangxiang rivers.
For one who has arrived for a brief visit, the attendant holds the torch and says: "Birth is like putting on a shirt; death is like taking off trousers.
If the attendant has realized Zen, when has there ever been anything to transmit? On the road, one does not leave home; at home, one does not leave the road.
Fire is hot, wind moves, water is moist, and earth is solid.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "When one does not seek the Buddha, does not seek the Dharma, and does not seek the Sangha, what then?
The Master said, "Remove the dust and grime before your face. The monk stepped forward and said, "In that case, one may wander freely through India and this land as one pleases.
The Master said, "Give me back the money for my straw sandals. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "Three days..."
Five days after the previous day, if one does not brandish the sword, the fisherman will nest in his hut. To speak in such a manner is very much like carrying water to the riverbank to sell it.
Light does not illuminate objects; objects do not exist either. When both light and objects have vanished, what is it then? Master Dahui said:
"The monastery remains for a thousand years, but the monks change every morning. [The Master] strikes the *zhuzhang* (staff) and says: "Bamboo shadows sweep the steps, yet there is no dust."
Immovable. The moon pierces the bottom of the pond; the water leaves no trace. Ascending the hall, he said:
"All dharmas are the Buddha-dharma. The lantern is itself the lantern; the pillar is itself the pillar.
All dharmas are not the Buddha-dharma. A shrimp swallows a great elephant; an earthworm bites a qilin to death. He then discerned the dragon.
"Seizing tigers and rhinoceroses like a snake—piercing through the nostrils of the monks of the world—I do not ask about that.
But beyond three thousand *li*, when meeting a person, you must not utter a single word in error. How would you say it? [He] drew a line with his staff and said:
"A single wild goose in the autumn stars; a thousand households with their mortars at night."

Ascending the hall: The golden wind fans the wilds; the jade dew hangs like pearls. Leaves fall amidst the trees; crickets chirp by the steps. The gate of liberation stands wide open, its eight characters revealed;
the meaning of reality extends throughout the ten directions. All of you see with your eyes and hear with your ears—each and every one surpassing the present and excelling the past.
Yet upon the single path that points directly upward, there is a further point of ambiguity: I would break your waist if you do not grasp it. First of all, do not take it...
Come. What you bring forth is not like it. It would shave your tongue bald. Standing like a sheer cliff ten thousand fathoms high, there is no room for deliberation.
To forge a sword, one must have the iron of Bīnzhou.

On the occasion of thanking the former guest master, he ascended the hall and said: "Striking the void produces sound; rare indeed is the one who recognizes the true note. Striking wood yields no sound; difficult is it to act."
When Xinghua saw a fellow practitioner, he drove him down from the Dharma Hall; when Gaoting visited Deshan, he departed upon seeing the flagpole.

These were all cases of failing to distinguish gold from sand or burning both jade and stone together; failing to differentiate the heterodox from the orthodox, the fault lies with the shadow of the whip.
Do you all know where Baiyun has fallen? [He] struck the meditation seat and descended.
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Kāśyapa’s rag-robe is worth hundreds of thousands of myriads; the jewel from the crown of a Wheel-Turning King is not worth half a penny.
Great assembly, when the ancients spoke thus, it may be said that their kindness is great and difficult to repay. He descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall on the Mid-Autumn Festival: Today is the fifteenth day of the eighth month; it is precisely the season of Mid-Autumn.
The moon above heaven is full, yet the moon among men is waning. Swallowing three or four—there is no sinew in one’s eyes. Spitting out seven or eight.
There is no tongue in one’s mouth. Nowadays, those everywhere are deliberating and all say: "At Vulture Peak they spoke of the moon; at Caoxi they pointed to the moon;
Mazu, Baizhang, and Nanquan enjoyed the moon. Little do they realize that this is precisely the second moon. Suddenly, there is a man...
[The Master] came out and said, "What is the first moon? He replied to him, "I truly know that you are making your living inside a ghost cave.
Ascending the hall, he cited Master Dongshan, who said: "To have words within words is called a dead phrase; to have no words within words..."
This is called a "live word. O practitioners of Chan, what is a live word? At this point, it is truly difficult to find anyone who has attained it.
Furthermore, it is said: "In practicing Chan, one must practice the live word; do not practice the dead word.
If you can realize it under a live word, you are fit to be a teacher to gods and men; if you realize it under a dead word, you will not even be able to save yourself. Master Linji said: "I..."

This is the living meaning of the Patriarchs. Therefore, although he asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma three times, he was struck three times like being brushed with a bundle of mugwort.
If one does not investigate the "living word," how could it be so? The ancients were like this.
Now it is not so. The word of death is itself the word of life; the word of life is itself the word of death. As for this life:
it does not abide when caged, nor does it turn its head when called. The ancient sages made no arrangements for it, and to this day it has no fixed location.
"His death was not a phenomenon of the present moment; it was not something reached by the ears or eyes. Seek it at the tips of the hundred grasses;
recognize your own self amidst the bustling marketplace. The spiritual source is bright and pure; its branches and tributaries flow on in secret.
He gave a shout and said, "Even an enlightened monk cannot comprehend this."

Ascending the hall, [the Master] drew four vertical lines and three horizontal lines; he took up one and let go of seven. Like a flash of lightning and a roll of thunder, it was like a collapsing cliff and splitting rocks.
Bowing to the Vajra Deity, one could not exert even the full power of one's strength. Why is it so? One who understands the Dharma fears.
On the anniversary of the Patriarch Bodhidharma’s passing, he held up the incense and said: “Coming, he did not come by way of the fundamental; departing, he did not depart by way of the fundamental.
With both hands he makes empty fists; opening his mouth, he falls into the secondary. Heh! Heh! Heh! How rare! Upon the peak of Mount Xionger, flowers bloom upon an iron tree.”
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "As for the Buddha-dhyāna and the Patriarch-dhyāna: if you understand them, you move freely in and out amidst the red dust of the mundane world;

if you do not understand them, you remain in the ghost-cave beneath the Black Mountains, waiting for donkey-year. This Dharma abides in its own station; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant."
For what reason did Old Śākyamuni lose his nostrils? The Great Master Bodhidharma came from Western India to transmit the mind-seal of the Supreme Vehicle (*agrayāna*).
Do you all recognize those of the Supreme Vehicle? [The Master] throws down his staff and says:
"Bodhisattvas of the Supreme Vehicle have no doubt; those of middle or lower capacity will surely find it strange upon hearing this."
Ascending the hall on the Winter Solstice, a monk asked, "Who is it that does not follow the waxing and waning of yin and yang, nor the shifting of the four seasons?
The Master said, "The old monk is beneath your feet. The monk stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then the student is at fault.
The Master said, "This is also what I use constantly. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "When the masses of yin are completely stripped away, [all things] cease."
The three mysterious halberds and armor are at the tips of the hundred grasses; a single breath secretly returns. The five ranks of ruler and subject are arrayed beyond the thousand sages:
where there is a Buddha, one must not dwell; where there is no Buddha, one must hurry past. In one stroke, forty-nine.
Ascending the hall, he said: "To open one's mouth is error; to conceive a thought is deviation. Master Langya Huijue said, 'Su Wu did not accept the prostrations of the Shanyu.
Do you all understand? For Langya to speak thus is also to have words that differ from his heart. He descended from the seat.
Ascending the hall, he cited Master Wuzu, who said: "There is a thing in the world that belongs neither to the mundane nor to the sagely;

it belongs neither to the heterodox nor to the orthodox. When all matters confront it, it naturally issues its commands. The Master remarked: "Once bitten by a snake, one fears even seeing a broken well-rope."
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "The ancients said, 'I do not dare to slight you; you shall all become Buddhas. Baiyun says:
'I do not dare to slight you, but you must each practice for yourselves. If I were to teach you to recite the Buddha's name, that would be slandering the Buddha.
If I were to teach you to contemplate the Dharma, that would be slandering the Dharma. If I were to teach you to contemplate the Sangha, that would be slandering the Sangha. To slander the Buddha..."
"To slander the Dharma and slander the Sangha is to deserve rebirth in the Avīci Hell. Nevertheless, Baiyun’s saying this is merely the old habit of his lips.
He ascended the hall and, citing Yunmen, said: "If there is anyone who can ask a question, bring forth one question! A monk came forward and bowed.
[Yunmen] said, "I ask the Master to examine this. Yunmen said, "Casting the hook to catch the giant fish (kūn-jing); yet he caught nothing but a shrimp.
The Master said, "Although Yunmen acted like 'releasing the hawk upon seeing the rabbit,' when scrutinized, he suffered no small loss. I, this mountain monk, am not like that.
If there is anyone who can pose a question, bring forth a question! When a monk stepped forward, [the Master] immediately said to him, "Three lives, six..."
Ten kalpas. Ascending the hall:
"A fine day is shared by many; one stroke, two victories. Yunmen’s fan leaps up to the thirty-third heaven and strikes the nose of Śakra.
Zhaozhou’s story about the dog having no Buddha-nature has been cast aside. Eat!
"Having finished eating the congee, go wash the alms bowl. How do you all understand this? If you do not understand, you fail Zhaozhou.
On the first day of the year, he ascended the hall and said, "All worthy sages are distinguished by means of the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*).
He raised his staff and said, "This is the staff; what is the unconditioned dharma? After a long silence, he said, "Jingqing."
The Way has existence; the clear teaching says the Way is non-existent. A stone mortar in mid-air; a gourd on the water.
Entering the hall, Yunmen said: "I have a phrase; I do not dare hope that you will understand it.
How will you bring it forth? Baizhang said: "I have a phrase; I do not dare hope that you will bring it forth. How will you understand it? One sits, seven walk.
Set it aside. Four verticals and three horizontals placed together. Going east, going west—like a well looking at a donkey.
South Mountain, North Mountain—like an ox pulling a millstone. *He lets out a shout.*
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "Mañjuśrī is the teacher of the seven Buddhas;
I wonder, what Buddha does Mañjuśrī take as his own? The Master said, "One blow for two counts. The monk pressed further, "From ancient times to the present, nothing has ever fallen away;
it is clearly right before our eyes. The Master said, "I grant you thirty blows. He then said: "Is the Way distant? It is true in every encounter. Are the sages distant? Their essence..."
Thus it is divine. Remove eight *liang* from the left eye; discard half a *jin* from the right eye.

Without raising the hand of Guliang, it is difficult to split the verdant heights of Mount Taihua. Only by exhausting the strength of the vast ocean can one support the treasure beneath the chin of the black dragon.
After a long silence, he said: "Rare are the guests who pierce their ears; many are those who mark the boat."
Ascending the hall on the Buddha’s Birthday: "The Buddha appeared in the world for the sake of one great cause and condition.
The mountains, rivers, and the great earth let out a great lion’s roar, expounding the Mahāprajñāpāramitā. Holding up his staff, he said: 'Look! Look!
He has entered the Deer Park once again.'"
Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the case of Yunmen, who said: "The ancient Buddha and the pillar meet in mutual penetration—what stage of capacity is this?
Yunmen himself provided a substitute answer: "Clouds rise on the southern mountain; rain falls on the northern mountain. Wuzu Huichao commented:
"How small-hearted Yunmen was all along! Sifan, however, says it otherwise: "The ancient Buddha and the pillar meet in mutual penetration—this is the fourth stage. The Master said:
"Lengthening the long to supplement the short—this is not without Yunmen. Buying a hat to fit the head—this returns it to Wuzu. Baiyun was not like this:
'The ancient Buddha intersects with the pillar'—what kind of function is that? One, two, three, four, five. He further said:
"One, two, three, four, five; it strikes the drum that shakes the heavens. Old Dharmatrāta, that hairy barbarian, stubbornly insists he is not the Patriarch! *Shout!*
With one shout, he descended from the seat.
First, the Dharma robes of King Yuhwang arrived. He ascended the hall and said: "The Eye of the True Dharma shatters the sand pot.

A single word encompasses the ten thousand phenomena; a single phrase settles heaven and earth. He carries out the command not transmitted by Buddhas and patriarchs, and expands the gate unverified by humans and devas. Huangbo—
How could the tip of a staff suffice to illuminate the great matter of Linji? How could Ba’ing’s three phrases repay the immense kindness of Yunmen?
Have you not seen it? A monk asked Master Damei, "What did you obtain upon seeing the Great Master Mazu that you settled on this mountain?
Damei said, "When I saw him tell me, 'This very mind is Buddha,' I immediately..."
[The monk] stayed there. The monk said, "Lately, Master, the Buddha-dharma has become something else again.
Mei asked, "What do you mean? The monk said, "Neither mind nor Buddha. Mei said, "This old fellow will continue to delude the men and women of this house for days to come.
He says 'neither mind nor Buddha,' while I say 'this very mind is Buddha. Great Old Mei is like a dragon that has gained the water."
Like a tiger relying on a mountain; were it not for a profound discernment of the wind from whence it comes, one would inevitably suffer its delusions.
Here at Baiyun, fortunately, Xian Yuyang has already passed away. It is truly like a wild goat hanging from a horn—no trace whatsoever remains.
You people here, for thirty years to come, do not go about confusing others!

Ascending the hall, he said: "To not set oneself in opposition to a single dharma is the Samādhi of Non-contention. When ten thousand elephants cannot conceal it, what hinders one from walking alone through the Great Square?
Seizing the tiger’s head and gathering its tail, there is no evasion and no taking up of responsibility.
After a long silence, he said: "Indeed, tonight's moon—there is nowhere its pure light does not reach."

Ascending the hall for the end of the summer retreat: On the fifteenth day of the fourth month, and on the fifteenth day of the seventh month—counting on one’s fingers, exactly ninety days have passed.
[The Master] suddenly grasps his staff and says: "It pierces through the nostrils of Śākyamuni Buddha.
All Tathāgatas of the past have already accomplished this gate; all Bodhisattvas of the present now each enter perfect clarity; those who practice in the future..."
Students, you should rely upon this Dharma. This Dharma is fundamentally and spontaneously perfected:

east, west, south, north, the four intermediate directions, above, and below—extending seven ways vertically and eight ways horizontally, there is nowhere it does not reach. Good assembly, its binding is thus, and its unbinding is thus.

You must skillfully protect and uphold this Dharma. For those of superior capacity, a single resolution brings all to completion; for those of middling and inferior capacity, there is much more to do.
They hear much, yet they do not believe. [Master] Zhuo strikes the sounding block once.
Regarding the Emperor’s viewing of the Tripitaka and the concluding ceremony, he ascends the hall and says: "It is not the character 'one,' nor is it the character 'eight.

The entire Great Canon of the Buddha’s Teachings is fully present before you right now. Without leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he has already descended into the royal palace; the Dharma-body of all Buddhas is constantly manifest."
Manifesting thus, he took the boundless substance of empty space as his true body and the indestructible mountain of adamant as his mountain of longevity.
How majestic! He manifested the virtue of Shun throughout the Nine Categories; how vast! He spread the imperial wind to the eight extremities of the world.
The unconditioned recluses beneath the forest trees all received the grace of rain and dew, while the aged, the young, the orphaned, and the weak among the people were all...

Inheriting the governance of a great era of peace and prosperity, the codes and regulations are fully established and the cultural refinements are renewed. The sun of Yao shines alongside the sun of the Buddha;
the golden wheel and the Dharma wheel turn eternally. Zhaozhou said: "The void may be measured and the wind may be bound, yet none can exhaustively describe the Buddha’s merit.
Again, he raised the case where a monk asked Muzhou: "When one breath turns the entire Great Canon of Teachings..."
"How is it? Mu asked. "What kind of *bi-luo-chui* (meat pie) do you have? Quickly bring it here! The Master said, "This monk possesses a mechanism as swift as a rushing torrent or a falling blade;
although Muzhou’s response was born of desperation, it nonetheless lacks the principles of the Buddha-dharma."
At this White Cloud Monastery, for twenty days starting from the first day of the month, we have been reciting the *Nianzang Jing*. On the twenty-sixth day, the ceremony was concluded.
Among the one hundred and seventy monks, each person was fully endowed with the entire canon of five thousand and forty-eight scrolls; every character was perfect and complete.
They turned the surging waves of the ocean of nature and revealed the sun and moon of the sky of meaning. Now tell me: is this the same as Muzhou, or is it different?
After a long silence, he said, "The text below is lengthy; we shall leave it for another day. He descended from his seat. Ascending the hall, he said:
"Since the eye and mind are identical, one sees upon the very first glance. To cite the ancients and then cite the present is, from the beginning, a lack of skillful means.
A single palm does not sound recklessly; a single thread does not form a seam. Picking up a single hair-tip, the lion is complete."
The Master appeared. He descended from his seat.

The donor invited him to ascend the hall. A monk asked, "The path beyond the ordinary, not transmitted by the thousand sages—today, as the lay patrons have gathered before you, we pray that the Master will proclaim it.
The Master said, "In spring, there are not three days of clear weather. The monk stepped forward and said, "It may truly be said that throughout past and present, there has been none [like this]."
"Fallen! It is clearly right before your eyes. The Master said, "A cricket in the fire has three eyes. The student asked, "Let us set aside this matter for a moment;
as for when a monk asked Zhaozhou, 'What is the Way? and Zhaozhou replied, 'That which is outside the wall'—what was the meaning of this?"
The Master said, "Look up and you see the sky; look down and you see the earth. The monk asked, "I am not asking about this path.
The Master said, "What path are you asking about? The monk said, "The Great Path. The Master said, "The Great Path penetrates Chang'an; what then?
The Master [Zhaozhou] said, "Sailing on the wind at sea, a boat upon the mountain. The monk asked, "As for the student’s question today—"
"Venerable Master, what is the Way? I do not yet know how to respond to this. The Master said, "Look straight down. The monk stepped forward and said, "In the past it was Zhaozhou;
today it is you, Master. The Master said, "Do not pretend to be clever. The monk bowed.

The Master then said, "Buddha to Buddha, hand to hand. In the realms of boundless lands, self and other are not separated by even a hair’s breadth. From patriarch to patriarch, it has been transmitted thus."
Throughout the ten ages of past and present, beginning and end never depart from the present moment. The supreme path above has not been transmitted by a thousand sages;
even if one were to sit and cut off the heads of both the Reward-body and Transformation-body Buddhas, one would still not escape falling into the heap of sounds and forms.

To further seek the profound wind beyond the limit of awe-inspiring sound, or to clarify the self alone prior to the empty kalpa, is much like striking one’s own palm with one’s fist through a leather shield.
Scratching an itch—what joy is there in that? Therefore it is said: "The myriad spirits share a single source; they are provisionally named 'Buddha.
When the substance is exhausted and the form dissolves, they do not perish; when the metal flows and the raw ore scatters, they remain ever-present.

The common people use them daily yet remain unaware; the Buddhas always know them and alone make use of them. By means of this principle of solitary use without partiality, they eternally abide before all forms."
With a mind that is unaware of daily activities, one stands far beyond the realm of ultimate truth. Without before or after, without past or present, self and other are merged as one;
the sage and the ordinary are no different. At such a time, how is it? "The green mountains do not lock the soaring momentum;
the vast blue sea surely knows its source is high. (He strikes the whisk and descends from the seat.)
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "In early summer it is gradually warm; in midsummer it is scorching hot. As a student who has come before you, I wish to hear the essential points of the Dharma.
The Master said, "In early summer it is gradually warm; in midsummer it is scorching hot. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "In early summer it is gradually warm;
in midsummer it is scorching hot. In the mountain hermitage at night, the cold is like ice; the rain marks the season of the yellow plum blossoms. Xuefeng’s neck..."
"One hundred and twenty catties of iron shackles—why not cast them off? The scale has no star at its tail.
Nanquan raised a water buffalo from his youth and said, "I have tamed it thoroughly. To seek iron on the point of a needle. Descend from the seat.

Ascending the hall for the commencement of the summer retreat: It is now the beginning of the first summer; the three-month *varṣā* (rainy season) retreat is being observed. In both the Western Heaven and this land, there is nothing but cause for celebration.
Holding up his staff, he said: "The Elder Śākyamuni is right now upon the tip of Baiyun’s staff, emitting a great radiance and expounding the Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra.
If, within this, there were even a single word or a single phrase that did not accord with you all—"
"To extract the nails and pull out the wedges, to untie the adhesions and remove the bonds—if I do not vow to attain perfect enlightenment, [so be it].
Yet, even though this is so, it only accounts for half. What is that other half? He struck the meditation staff and said, "The heavens are vast; the earth is vast."
The Master ascends the hall for the ceremony of offering to the ten thousand Buddhas. "In the three realms there is no dharma; where can one seek the mind? The four elements are originally empty;
upon what does the Buddha rely to dwell? An arrow is fixed upon a mulberry tree; sap flows from a willow tree. A catfish climbs a bamboo pole;
a swift falcon cannot catch it up. Raising his whisk, he says: "Look! Look! There are worlds that take fragrant food as the Buddha-work."
There are worlds where the Buddha’s work is performed through sound; there are worlds where the Buddha’s work is performed through all places;

and there are worlds where the Buddha’s work is performed through fragrant food, such that people there certainly cannot eat. Where the Buddha’s work is performed through sound, people there certainly cannot hear it.
Where the Buddha’s work is performed through all places, it even extends to the white clouds as its eyebrows and whiskers.
To fall into decline—how can this ultimately be? A scale is not equal to a ruler.
When a donor invites the Buddha to ascend the seat for ten thousand Buddhas, the Buddha is not distant from people; it is realized within the very mind.
From where is this news obtained? The Dharma has no attachment; it arises only by relying on conditions. One must strictly avoid sitting here. O clever ones, as soon as...
Upon hearing this, it is raised up: like a golden-winged bird parting the sea to seize and swallow a dragon directly; like a lion roaming about without seeking a companion.
It is thus in every dust mote; it is thus in every thought-moment. The whole body comes in this way; the whole body abides in this manner. Have you not seen?
Formerly, King Prasenajit asked the Buddha: "Within the ultimate truth (paramārtha-satya), is there still the conventional truth (saṃvṛti-satya)? If one says..."
If it exists, wisdom should not be one; if one says it does not exist, wisdom should not be two. As for the meaning of "one" and "two," what is that meaning? The Buddha said:
"In the past, during the time of Dragon Light Buddha, you once asked about this meaning. I have nothing further to say now."
"You now have neither hearing nor speech; this lack of hearing and speech is called the 'one meaning' and the 'two meanings.

For kalpas as numerous as motes of dust, the Elder Śākyamuni accomplished this unsurpassed Dharma-King’s dhāraṇī-gate, yet it was shattered into a hundred fragments by a single blow from King Prasenajit.
More than two thousand years have passed since then, and it has simply been impossible to gather back. Today, I shall compassionately save it."
The assembly opens; the faithful gather. Although there is no such exchange of questions and answers, the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*) manifests vast and open before them.

Nothing is lacking in practice; nothing is incomplete in principle. This is what is called the convergence of immeasurable excellence, wherein the knowledge and vision of liberation (*vimukti-jñāna-darśana*) universally perfumes all.
Nevertheless, one must not let this pass before those with clear eyes. Such a thing is easy [to do], yet it is not permissible.
Thus it is difficult; thus it is difficult. Not thus, it is easy. Clearly at the tips of the hundred grasses, clearly is the meaning of the Patriarch.
The entire earth is the patron of Old Master Wáng. This is not deceiving you all.
Before Layman Páng had seen Mázǔ, where did his nose and its string fall? After a long silence, he struck the whisk and said:
When the third-tier waves rise high, the fish transform into dragons; yet fools still bail out the water from the night pond.

For the Assembly for the Offering to the Myriad Buddhas, I ascend the hall. Recently, you brothers have taken up the task of constructing and providing for this Way-place for the Offering to the Myriad Buddhas;
all of this is nothing other than manifesting the Buddha-work to benefit sentient beings throughout the entirety of the ten directions, the void, and the pervasive Dharma.
In this realm, all Buddhas of the three periods of time have departed after receiving offerings. Only Śākyamuni, the Elder, thought to himself:
"This is no easy matter; it is truly difficult. It would be better to pour molten copper into my mouth than to accept food from one who offers with faith;
it would be better to wrap my body in glowing iron than to accept clothing from one who offers with faith. O Great Assembly, since he was indeed Śākyamuni, the Elder...
This is a most extraordinary perspective. These words are like kicking a ball in a bustling marketplace;
one must have eyes that see clearly and hands that discern, knowing before the movement has even been raised—swift as the wind and rapid as lightning.

If you hesitate to deliberate and reflect, there is no connection at all. As the ancients said: "The single path before the sound—you must penetrate and clarify it for yourself; after the phrase, it is not..."
He has come, yet he still falls short by half; not even a speck of dust can penetrate, as if separated by the Iron Ring Mountains. Meeting so wondrously, with what shall we interrogate one another?
Striking the meditation seat, he said: "A flash of lightning opens the eyes of a thousand sages; the best mountains are mostly found on the highest peaks."
Ascending the hall: This morning is the fifteenth day of the fifth month. Strike up Nanquan’s broken drum! Everyone sees it with their eyes and hears it with their ears;
even the pillar and the lantern dance in joy. As for Nanquan’s saying, "Old Teacher Wang does not strike this broken drum"—how do you all deliberate upon this?
Nowadays, when people hear this, they often ask, "Why does he not strike it?"
Fools like these are called "shaveling soldiers who plunder rice and gruel. What use are they? If Baiyun were to let them pass, he would inevitably be held accountable by those in all quarters;
therefore, with his staff, he struck them all down at once.
Ascending the hall at the conclusion of the summer retreat: Yesterday it was thus; today it is thus. Throughout the ninety days of this summer, what great heat has there been?
The insects by the ruined walls have only now begun to chirp; the leaves of the autumn forest are only now falling.
Taking up this head of dead firewood, let us for now turn toward the smokeless flame. (He strikes the whisk and descends from the seat.)
Ascending the hall, he took up his staff and said: "The entire great earth, when gathered together, is as large as a grain of millet.

When the ancients reached this point, what such desperate urgency was there? 'The Dharma abides in its own station; the characteristics of the world are eternally constant. Fire flows westward; water heads east. [He planted the staff] and said:
'In all manner of arrangements, none surpasses the ordinary. To be as usual is just like the arrival of the autumn wind.'"
Descend from your seats.
Ascending the hall for the Emperor’s Birthday: With a single word I offer congratulations on his boundless longevity; the great earth, its mountains, and rivers proclaim it aloud.
Last night, gazing from the summit of Mount Zhurong, I saw that upon the branches of the ancient pines, new growth has once again been added.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] raised the following case: When Yangshan was thanking Zhongyi for his ordination, Zhongyi, from atop his meditation seat, clapped his hands over his mouth and said, "He-he.
Yangshan moved from west to east; Zhongyi again clapped his hands over his mouth and said, "He-he.
Yangshan moved from east to west, then stood in the middle before thanking him for the ordination. Zhongyi asked, "Where did you obtain this samādhi? Yangshan replied, "Cao..."
Xituo held up his seal and presented it. Baoying said, "Tell me, at Caoxi, with what kind of person did you employ this samādhi?
Foshan said, "I employed it for Yixiu Jue. Shanshan then asked, "Where did you receive this samādhi, Master?
Baoying said, "I received this samādhi from Master Mazu. The Master said, "Zhongyi, slapping your mouth, 'He-he'—this is not it."
The Great Master Mazu attained this samādhi at that place; Yangshan moved from west to east and from east to west.
This samādhi was certainly not attained at Caoxi. Since it was not there, tell me: from where did he attain this samādhi?
The ancients were resolute and their words were never uttered in vain. You all must realize this for yourselves before you can succeed.
Ascending the hall for the opening of the furnace: When the season arrives, its principle naturally manifests. The sun does not wait for fire to be hot; the moon does not wait for wind to be cool.
The world is ten feet wide; the ancient mirror is ten feet wide; the brazier is ten feet wide. The Buddha is vast and the mud is much;
the boat is high as the waters rise. Descend from the seat.
Ascending the hall, a monk asked, "What is it like at seventy-three or eighty-four? The Master said, "Śākyamuni has entered into your nostrils.
The monk bowed. The Master then said, "I do not ask about seventy-three or eighty-four;
but as for this sentence, 'Śākyamuni has, for no reason, entered into your nostrils'—how would you say it? Liang.
Jiuyun said: "The waters of the sea do not produce ice. He descended from his seat.
He ascended the hall and cited the case of Xinghua, who, while at Sansheng, often said to people:
"I have traveled throughout the south on pilgrimage once, yet with my staff I never once struck upon anyone who truly understands the Buddha-dharma. What are you doing here?"
When Shengwen heard of this, he asked Huazhu, "What kind of eye do you possess? Huazhu let out a shout. Shengwen said, "It must be you who can achieve it. Huazhu then withdrew.
Upon hearing this, Dajue remarked, "This is the karma accumulated over many lifetimes; the wind of that karma has blown it into my gate.
Later, Huazhu went to Dajue’s monastery and served as the head of the administrative office (*yuanzhu*). One day, Dajue called out to him, "Head of the office, I have heard of you..."
"I have traveled all over the south practicing the Way, yet I have never encountered a single person who has grasped the Buddha-dharma with their staff.
What kind of eye do you possess? Hua gave a shout. Jue raised his staff. Hua hesitated; Jue struck him.
Hua shouted again; Jue struck him once more. The next day, as Hua was passing in front of the Dharma Hall, Jue called out, "Warden! I am directly—"
"I suspect you were given two blows yesterday. Try to explain it to me.
Huaihai said, "I learned a phrase regarding guest and host from Master Sansheng, but I have been completely defeated by my elder brother here. Please grant me a Dharma-gate of peace and ease."
Jue said: "This blind fellow has come here to suffer defeat. Take off your patched robe and give him a thorough beating!
Only through being transformed by the staff will he thoroughly see the principle of how Linji received blows from Huangbo. The Master said:
"Xinghua’s bearing was like that of a king; why was it only at the tip of Dajue’s staff that he finally saw Linji receiving blows from Huangbo?"
As for the principle underlying this staff: my monk’s fly-whisk has traveled throughout the four quarters of the world;
whoever it strikes shall be one who understands the Buddha-dharma. This will spare us from mutual neglect in days to come.
On the first day of the year, the Master ascended the hall. A monk asked, “The year is new, the moon is new, and the days are new; there is nothing that is not renewed.
At this very moment, we pray that the Master will offer a blessing for the Emperor.
The Master said, “Heaven revolves to the left and Earth revolves to the right. The monk stepped forward and said, “Behold the new edicts before you; let everyone [hearken].”

"Congratulating you on ten thousand years of joy. The Master said, "Who is the one who knows this? The student advanced and asked, "A monk asked Mingjiao, 'Is there still Buddha-dharma at the beginning of the new year?
Mingjiao replied, 'No. What was the meaning of this? The Master said, "It struck right on his nostrils."
The student said, "As for Jingqing saying 'there is,' how is that? The Master said, "It would burn your tongue to the marrow.
The student said, "One person says there is, and another says there is not; are they singing in unison with the same tune, or is there something else to be deliberated upon?
The Master said, "Neither is it like that. The student said, "If so, then every year is a good year, and every day is a good day."
The Master said, "How many people are sitting right here? A monk stepped forward and said, "A master of clear eyes naturally possesses it.
The Master said, "That, too, is unnecessary. The monk bowed. The Master then said, "Today is the beginning of the New Year;
yesterday was the end of the Old Year. Year after year, one simply follows along with it. If only one’s body and mind are at peace, that is the Buddha-dharma."
There is nothing that is not so. Yet, for those who have left the household life, there is nothing that is not a state of peace and bliss.

From the daily routines of rising and sitting, eating and drinking, to the movements of turning, bending, and bowing—how could these not be the field of peace and bliss? The cawing of crows and the chirping of sparrows can accord with the true source;
the movement of wind and the flying of dust all manifest the Buddha-work. Striking the incense stand with his staff, he said: "All Buddhas of the three periods of time are entirely present here."
In this very place, the dragon girl immediately attained Buddhahood; it was not that Shanxing was born only to fall into ruin.
When the Dharma-heir Baozang and the Dharma-heir Tancang ascended to the hall, withered wood met spring and one could see the five petals of the flower bloom;
cold ashes sent forth flames, naturally reaching the point of consuming the plains. To observe victory or defeat, why rely on the movement of chess pieces? One need only aspire to the Great Square.

Toiling his noble steed, he gazes upon these springs and rocks where the monastic community is desolate. Were it not for meeting with a man of realization, who would have heard the resonance of metal and jade?
Yunmen let out three blows of the staff at Dongshan; Linji’s True Dharma Eye was extinguished by a blind donkey;
Deshan turned his back on the Dharma Hall and departed wearing straw sandals; and Zhuyou visited Zhaozhou and leaned upon his staff. Immediately—

Go! As for the patriarchs of old—whether Buddhas or Ancestors—who cast out hooks and laid snares, each claimed for themselves that they were like dragons leaping and tigers bounding, displaying every bit of their majestic ferocity and meeting the enemy with full force.
Yet, in truth, not even a hair’s breadth of actual reality was seen. At such a time, what is it?
When the nine-myriad-li Peng bird merely spreads its wings, the thousand-year-old crane immediately soars aloft.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Where there is a Buddha, do not dwell; where there is no Buddha, run past with all haste. Three thousand miles away, one plucks the willow blossoms.
The nostrils of the patch-robed monk point their great heads downward. He suddenly took up his staff and said: "Alala! Alala!"
In spring, there are not three days of clear weather; travelers on the roads are few.
Entering the hall: A thousand waves competing to rise is the family style of Mañjuśrī; a single expanse of clear sky is the bed of Samantabhadra.
The wind is gentle and the sun is warm; the willows are green and the flowers are red. What kind of realm is this? [The Master] raises his staff and says:
"It is you all—wading through the red dust, entering the villages, with the sun and moon slung across your shoulders and Mount Sumeru carried upon your backs. Thirty years from now..."
Do not fail those who place their trust in you. Master Zhuo descends from the seat.

Entering the summer retreat, I ascend the hall: fundamentally there is no cultivation or realization; what need is there for a long-term duration? To bring blessings in accordance with the season, we observe the three-month *an-ju* (summer retreat).
The Unsurpassed Dharma King possesses a great *dhāraṇī* gateway called Perfect Enlightenment (*Vimalakīrti-nirdeśa*). From it flow forth all pure *tathatā*, bodhi, and nirvāṇa.
The crane’s leg is naturally long; the duck’s leg is naturally short. [He] plants his staff and lets out a roar.

At the conclusion of the distribution of the Tripitaka, he ascended the hall and said: "In the teachings it is said that all the eighty-four thousand dharma-treasuries of verbal instruction expounded by the Tathāgata are called 'words' (wén).
To be free from all sounds, voices, and written characters, such that the principle cannot be expressed—this is called 'meaning' (yì)."

Furthermore, it is said: "If, among the various sūtras, the words and phrases are extensive and can cause the minds of sentient beings to leap with joy, these are called 'provisional meaning' (neyārtha).
If they can proclaim that both words and mind are like ashes, these are called 'definitive meaning' (nītārtha), O Great Assembly."
Once you have caused the minds and intentions of sentient beings to leap with joy, they will surely be able to depart from all delusive conditions.

When delusive conditions are departed from, one is immediately the Buddha of Suchness (*tathatā*). Why, then, is this called "provisional meaning" (*neyārtha*)? Sentient beings and their mental states are like ashes;
ultimately, what is there to be understood? Within seven days in the White Cloud Mountains, I perused the entire Great Canon (*Tripitaka*), totaling five thousand [volumes].
In these forty-eight fascicles, for every phrase and every character, do not form the notion of a phrase, do not form the notion of a character,

do not form the notion of a composition, do not form the notion of speaking, do not form the notion of a Buddha, do not form the notion of one who is not a Buddha, and do not form the notions of definitive or non-definitive meaning.
The preceding exposition and praise constitute boundless roots of goodness, which are solely intended as a prayer for the long life and prosperity [of the Sovereign].
*May the Holy Life Be Ten Thousandfold Peace.* Compiled by *Qingyu*,
a student of the *Record of Sayings* from Kaiyuan Chan Monastery in Pingjiang Prefecture.
Entering the monastery, he pointed to the mountain gate and said: "When entering the gate, one sees the plaque; when mounting the horse, one sees the road. Great function manifests before one;

one strides alone across the crimson heavens. Taking up the memorial from the Xuanzheng Yuan, he said: "Entrusted in the Western Heaven, it circulates in this Eastern Land. The sun and moon are harbored within the breast; the breath is exhaled."
"A long rainbow. Where words cannot reach, he points to the Dharma seat and says:
"Above, one does not see the Buddhas; below, one does not see sentient beings; in between, one does not see oneself.
Only then may one ascend this seat. He then ascends, saying: "The thousand-year shadowless tree; now, the bottomless leather drum. Thus he ascends.
[The assembly] takes their seats.

After the ritual for the Emperor’s longevity is completed, Wanshou Wuheshang strikes the gavel and says: "O assembly of dragons and elephants upon this Dharma seat, you should contemplate the primary principle.
The Master then says: "As for contemplating the primary truth (*paramārtha-satya*), how is it to be contemplated? An ancient said: 'It is luminous within the mind and eyes...'"
Though they appear side by side, their forms cannot be seen; though they shine brightly within the realm of form, their principle cannot be divided.

Since they cannot be seen and cannot be divided, then the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind, as well as forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and mental objects, are all merely matters on the periphery of shadows.
In the ultimate truth (*paramārtha-satya*), there is no intersection whatsoever with them. If one can directly accept and take responsibility for this, [one realizes it].
The new Elder has today opened the hall and completed one term of his tenure. If this is not yet so, and you have doubts, please ask. At that time, a monk asked:
"When the three rounds of drums have ceased and the great assembly has all gathered, the student comes forward; we pray that the Master will offer a benediction for the Emperor.
The Master said: "The clouds clear and the sun and moon are bright; the snow melts and spring comes to heaven and earth. The monk stepped forward and said: "If it is thus, then the four seas..."

"All return within the Imperial Transformation; where among the myriad spirits would they not be touched by grace? The Master said, "Not even a single fraction less than what you, Upāsaka, have attained.
The student further asked, "As for the ancient saying: 'What falls is not another thing; wherever it extends, it is not dust.

Mountains, rivers, and the great earth—all reveal the body of the Dharma King. What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "Piercing through the summit and penetrating to the bottom. The student pressed on.
[The Master] said: "The wild scenery is no longer interrupted by mountains; the light of heaven directly communicates with the water. The Master added:
"If you wish to exhaust the view for a thousand li, climb yet another story. The monk bowed, and the Master said: "It turns out it has always been right here. Then he said:
"From the beginning at Deer Park to the end at the Bahudā River—in this interval between the two, [the Buddha] never spoke a single word."
"O Great Assembly! When Śākyamuni spoke thus, was he speaking or not speaking? Let us set aside for a moment whether he spoke or did not speak;
but as for his speaking in such a manner—does it truly accord with the ultimate matter of the School Gate?
He suddenly took up his staff and said: "To mention one, you must not mention two. To let one slip by is to fall into the second. "The heavens are high."
The earth is thick, the waters are vast, and the mountains are far away. When a single phrase is fully raised, the wind is calm and the waves are still. Holding up his staff, he said:
"Once every three thousand years, the Yellow River clears."
Ascending the hall, [the Master said]: "Light does not see darkness; darkness does not see light. When light and darkness are both forgotten—what a fine 'no-matter' monk! Master Ying’an said:
'When light and darkness are both forgotten, how is this any different from an ordinary worldly teacher?
If you all can recognize such an ordinary worldly teacher, he is precisely a 'no-matter' monk. If he is a 'no-matter' monk," [he is one who has realized this].
Thus one recognizes the common, worldly masters. For this reason, since the Buddhas appeared in the world and the Patriarchs came from the West, there has been nothing that is "this" or "not this.
While the heavens revolve to the left and the earth turns to the right, they join their palms at the mountain gate and burn incense within the Buddha hall;
the old monks of the world have their mouths hung up on the wall as they descend from their seats.
Ascending the hall, the Master raised an old case: A monk asked Nan-yuan, "On this ball of red flesh, it stands like a thousand-fathom cliff—is this not what you, the Master, have said?
Nan-yuan replied, "Yes. The monk then overturned the meditation seat. Nan-yuan said, "Look at this blind fellow making such a mess!
The monk hesitated, and Nan-yuan struck him. The Master said, "Nan-yuan was much like someone tripping on level ground. Although this monk..."
To gain an advantage is merely for a beggar to see small profit. Master Ying’an said: "If it were not for this monk, who would dare to pluck the tiger’s whiskers?
Who then would have seen the great merit of Nanyuan’s meritorious service? The thief is a petty person, yet his wisdom surpasses that of a gentleman."
Xie Dongzhai took up the whisk and ascended the hall to give a discourse: "That which is equal in regard to food is also equal in regard to the Dharma;
that is to say, this Dharma is equal, with no high or low. Yangqi’s 'Vajra Circle' and 'Thorny Bristles' cannot but be equal.
Dongshan’s 'Three Pounds of Hemp' and Yunmen’s 'Dry Shit-stick' cannot but be equal. Gold is tested by stone; jade is tested by fire."

[The Master] tested [the assembly]. The abbot’s staff member said, “I have heard that once one is full, one forgets a hundred hungers; today, this mountain monk’s own body is exactly like that. He descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, a monk asked, “What is it like when a single word expresses everything? The Master said, “A team of four horses cannot overtake the tongue. The monk pressed further, “As for learning...”
The monk said, "No one would. The Master said, "A head three feet long. The monk stepped forward and asked, "What is it like when one goes forth in this very way?
The Master said, "A monkey tying itself to a pillar. The monk bowed. The Master then said: "If you do not look back when the teaching is raised, you are already mistaken;
if you attempt to deliberate upon it, when will you ever awaken? The assembly, act according to this and there will be a place for entrustment. Do you understand? After the snow..."
Only now do I know the steadfast character of the pine and cypress; it is only when faced with difficulty that one sees the heart of a true man.

When the Buddha attained the Way, he ascended the hall [and said]: "The moon is in the sky, yet its reflection is contained in all waters. A single film over the eye causes empty flowers to fall in confusion.
Thus, Śākyamuni the Old Man has gone off to join the ranks of the water-buffaloes. Therefore it is said: "Obtained from..."
The mind: it would turn *eranda* into a sandalwood tree; yet it misses the essential point. Nectar becomes a garden of thorns.
Striking the meditation seat, he said, "No one understands this meaning; it makes me remember Nanquan."
Ascending the hall: This morning is the fifteenth day of the twelfth month. It is precisely the time to vie for precedence and behold it clearly.

Last night the snow darkened the vast sky; this morning the sun rises at high noon. Adding to and subtracting from, giving forth and gathering in—shifting the constellations and displacing the stars, transcending the present and surpassing antiquity.
Taking this very thing as the vehicle of our school, who would say that gold is like dung? (He lets out a shout and descends.)

[The Master] took his seat. Ascending the hall, he said: "This morning is the twentieth day of the twelfth lunar month; it is precisely the time to shift from the relaxed to the urgent. Do not let the year end and the season exhaust itself with deliberation on every matter.
This does not equal the way of the patch-robed monk: if you wish to walk, simply walk; if you wish to sit, simply sit. What is there [to deliberate]?"
[The assembly] deliberated. Master Zhuo said, "A shrimp cannot leap out of its basket.
He requested the Rector to ascend the hall. With a single blow of the mallet, he immediately realized it;
without relying on a single blow, he revealed the essential core of the patch-robed monks. Comparing this to Xinghua’s beating of Kebin or Linji’s departure from Huangbo, even today—
Separated by four or five hundred years, yet their total functioning appears and disappears; their wondrous application is纵横 (zōnghéng—unrestricted and pervasive).

Without the slightest blade being deployed, corpses lie strewn across ten thousand *li*. It is truly not separated by even a single hair’s breadth. But in the end, how is it so? Li Guang did not receive a fief as a marquis.
Ascending the hall, he said: "Ordinary people truly claim that things exist; those of the Two Vehicles analyze them and claim they do not exist; Pratyekabuddhas regard them as illusory existence;

and Bodhisattvas realize that their very substance is emptiness. As the Sutra says: 'If one sees me by means of form, or seeks me through sound, such a person walks upon a deviant path and cannot see the Tathāgata.'"
Ascending the hall, he said: "Empty-handed, one grasps a hoe; At the third watch, one passes through Bianzhou. Walking, one rides a water buffalo;
One roams the depths of the ocean floor. A person passes over the bridge; Leading an ox, one goes to pull at Mara. The bridge flows, yet the water does not flow;
A lantern ball hangs upon the tree. He descended from his seat.
Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "Before this mountain monk had even ascended this seat, Kāśyapa Buddha had already presented the discourse to all of you.

Now tell me, what Dharma was he speaking? 'Two breakages do not constitute one; the One-Dharma remains eternally present. If you understand it in terms of 'one' and 'two,' you will suffer in the depths of saṃsāra for eons.
He suddenly took up his staff and said: "Supported across the waters of the broken bridge, let us return together to the light."
The Recorded Sayings of Yuecun (Moon Village), Second Abbot of Kaiyuan Chan Monastery.
Compiled by the student Qingyu.

On the twelfth day of the sixth month in the first year of the Huangqing era, by imperial decree, [the Master] entered the temple. Having finished the opening of the hall and the offering of prayers for the Emperor, he took his seat.
A monk asked: "The heavens hang down a precious canopy; the earth wells up golden lotuses. The Buddhas of the three periods turn the Great [Dharma Wheel]..."
The Wheel of Dharma: may all sentient beings throughout the great earth attain perfect enlightenment.

This assembly on Vulture Peak is as solemn today as it was then. This student has come forward; I pray to hear your words of praise. The Master said: "The imperial foundation is vast and majestic throughout the three thousandfold world; the sagely virtue extends and flourishes for ten million years. The student further said:
"The Sovereign sits upright and effortless, transforming through non-action; the flowers of the five petals bloom, their fragrance pervading the entire realm. The Master said:
Exhausting all one's strength, one cannot bring it forth. A monk asked: "I recall Emperor Tongguang asking Xinghua: 'When I reclaimed the Central Plains, I obtained a treasure;
to this day, no one has offered a price for it. What was the meaning of this? The Master said: "The sun shines and heaven looks down."
